correctness.rationale: Theorem 6 was read in its primary full text, with all quantifiers and four conditions checked for (2,1,1,B,129,4). The finite base interval [129,324] and bad 128 are exhaustively certified by two independent subset-sum algorithms. The distinct-square induction extends coverage to every B>=18. A residue obstruction modulo Q_B=S_B+2 proves every hQ_B-1 impossible for arbitrary h>=1. Symbolic inequalities and index distinctness are proved, not extrapolated.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The earlier theorem does not cover arbitrary sparse sequence tails; the later ordinary-base bounds do not address false certificates for general A. The present result does not deny the narrower valid results.

originality.rationale: The 2015 printed Theorem 6 asserts a stronger universally quantified implication, which the displayed infinite counterexample family logically refutes. The prior 2014 certificate is limited to the full natural-number sequence; the later 2017 study is also in that domain. Full text and indexed-result searches did not identify a mathematically equivalent correction. The residual possibility of an unlocated erratum is expressly retained.
residual_risks: An unlocated erratum or equivalent earlier counterexample could alter the novelty verdict.

value.rationale: This is an unbounded family of false certificates for a central published completeness theorem, including the precise motivating square-power threshold and inequalities. It isolates a tail-availability condition missing from a generalization used as a certification method; the obstruction persists for strictly increasing positive-density gcd-one sequences. The structural modular argument is not a mere finite numerical discrepancy.
